title: Latency-aware soft-scaling ledger (regional GPU experiments, Jul 2026)
summary: Hands-on experiment ledger for a latency-driven soft-scaling policy across three regional GPU pools. Objective: reduce p95 latency tail events while minimizing cold-start and overprovision costs. This file captures raw experiment rows, short analysis and pragmatic recommendations for release candidates.

key_findings: Latency-first triggers (p95/p99) reduce observed tail incidents compared to QPS-only policies but can increase average cost unless paired with longer cool-downs and soft buffers.
Composite triggers (latency OR burst QPS) gave the best tradeoff in busy regions: faster detection of surge + fewer needless scale-ups on transient noise.
Derivative/velocity-based triggers (p95 derivative) prevented repeated flip-flopping during oscillatory bursts and reduced unnecessary scale-downs following short spikes.
Short probe intervals lowered detection latency but increased noise — probe cadence should be matched to expected workload spike shape and regional network jitter.

p99-based policies are effective for strict tail-SLO regions (enterprise customers) but materially increase unit cost and cold-start exposure; reserve larger min_replicas or warm pools for p99 use-cases.
Observed regional differences: eu-west1 benefitted more from longer cool-downs (lower variance), us-west1 required more aggressive warm-buffering due to higher burstiness in product traffic.
Max replica caps must be set per pool with a safety margin for cross-traffic (shared nodes) — hard max was hit in mixed-batch pool during E006 leading to queued requests and higher p99.
Overall cost deltas ranged -4% to +22% across runs: only E003 achieved cost savings while preserving latency targets; others increased cost but improved tail behavior.
No experiment caused a production outage; tail incidents are defined as >2 mins above target latency for >1% of requests in a 10-minute window.
Cold-start incidents tracked separately correlated with low min_replicas and use of p99 triggers — mitigations required for sensitive customers.
recommendations: Adopt composite triggers (latency OR burst-qps) as default for public hosted pools with region-specific thresholds.
Set region-specific cool_down_s: us-west1=120–180s, eu-west1=180–240s, ap-northeast1=150–210s based on noise profiles.
Introduce derivative-based gate to prevent scale-downs when recent latency velocity is positive; use this as an overlay to existing p95 triggers.
For p99-sensitive customers offer an SLA class with pinned warm-pool min_replicas and higher reserved capacity (dedicated or private deployments preferred).
Increase probe robustness: use median of 3 fast probes spaced 2s apart rather than single sample to reduce jitter-driven actions.
Limit max_replicas on mixed-batch pools OR add admission control to surface queued request indicators before hitting hard caps.
Run A/B for 2 weeks with 5% traffic using composite policy and warm-buffer to measure real production cost/latency impact before full rollout.
next_steps: Implement composite trigger in autoscaler branch and add telemetry hooks for per-trigger attribution (INF-1439).
Schedule 5% traffic A/B in us-west1 for 14 days starting 2026-08-01; owners: Maya Chen + Ravi Kapoor.
Create a warm-pool prototype for p99 SLA customers and document pricing impact for sales + SRE (confluence page draft).
Add experiment E007 to test admission-control alarms when pool reaches 85% queuing capacity to avoid hard max hits.
Sync with product for expected traffic shape changes (release calendar) and with SRE to tune probe schedules regionally.
notes: This ledger is intentionally concise — raw telemetry exports (csv) and dashboards referenced in linked_artifacts. Metrics definitions: p95/p99 measured at request-response end-to-end; avg_util_pct measured on CUDA utilization averaged across GPUs in pool. Cost delta is estimated tokenized unit cost vs baseline for same traffic window.
